title: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM): what it finds in stored data, how it differs from inline DLP, and what can be automated

prose.text: DSPM examines data at rest in cloud and on-premises stores, where inline DLP watches data in motion. {{what-it-is}}

prose.label: Against inline DLP.
prose.text: {{at-rest-vs-in-flight}} {{marketing-scope}} The help pages document onboarding for cloud accounts and on-premises stores: [[dspm.scanning:scope]]. It classifies with the same DLP engines and dictionaries as the rest of Zscaler DLP ([[dspm.scanning:classification]]), and DSPM appears as a channel of a DLP engine: [[zia.dlp.engines:engine-channels]].

prose.label: How it scans.
prose.text: Scope, onboarding, scanners, authentication and residency are in [[dspm.scanning]].
{{no-client-surface}} Whether DSPM has an admin API is open {{gap:api-and-scanner-contract}}.

prose.label: Onboarding.
prose.text: Cloud accounts are onboarded per provider in [[dspm.onboarding-aws]] (CloudTrail in [[dspm.onboarding-aws-cloudtrail]]), [[dspm.onboarding-azure]] (errors in [[dspm.onboarding-azure-errors]]) and [[dspm.onboarding-gcp]]; the orchestrator, network and account settings are in [[dspm.orchestrator]], [[dspm.network-configuration]] and [[dspm.cloud-accounts]].

prose.label: Scanning and services.
prose.text: Scan rules are in [[dspm.scan-rules]] and [[dspm.vulnerability-scanning]]; registered services and integrations in [[dspm.service-registration]], [[dspm.service-registration-databases]] and [[dspm.integrations]].

prose.label: Inventory and findings.
prose.text: Inventory, graphs, investigation and classification are in [[dspm.inventory]], [[dspm.graphs]], [[dspm.investigation]] and [[dspm.classification]]; alerts, policies, action rules, on-premises scanning and roles in [[dspm.alerts]], [[dspm.policies]], [[dspm.action-rules]], [[dspm.on-premises]] and [[dspm.roles]].

Answer DSPM automation questions as unsupported by any captured client or contract, and say the API question is open.

what-it-is.statement: DSPM is an AI-powered solution that protects data stored on-premises and in the cloud by continuously scanning it for misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and permissions that might contribute to attack vectors; it shows where sensitive data resides, classifies it, detects duplicate data and misconfigured stores holding it, and contextualizes exposure and posture.

quotes: Zscaler Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) is an AI-powered solution to protect your organization’s data stored on-premises and in the cloud
by continuously scanning the data for numerous potential misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and permissions that might contribute to attack vectors.

DSPM provides detailed insights into where this sensitive data resides in your cloud environment, identifies and classifies sensitive data, detects duplicate data and misconfigurations in data stores containing sensitive data, and contextualizes data exposure and security posture.

misconfigurations.statement: It scans data for issues such as data exposure, publicly exposed sensitive data, over-privileged access without proper RBAC, and sensitive data exposed to unmanaged services and models, and identifies policy violations at the resource and data level mapped to compliance frameworks.

quotes: Detect data misconfigurations: Scans data for any vulnerabilities such as data exposure, publicly exposed sensitive data, over-privileged access to data without proper role-based access control (RBAC), sensitive data exposed to unmanaged services and models, etc.
Apply security policies: Identifies security policy violations at the resource and data level. It also provides a complete mapping of security policies within various compliance frameworks.

prioritization.statement: It prioritizes risk by severity, with step-by-step remediation guidance and configurable near-real-time alerts and notifications.

quotes: DSPM aggregates security data and prioritizes risk based on severity, coupled with step-by-step remediation guidance and configurable, near-real-time alerts and notifications.

marketing-owasp-llm.statement: Zscaler's DSPM product page says it deep-scans AI models for vulnerabilities across the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, pinpointing vulnerabilities, misconfigurations and permissions, with step-by-step remediation guidance.

quotes: Risk Assessment Deep-scan AI models for vulnerabilities across the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs. Pinpoint vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and permissions, and remediate with step-by-step guidance.

at-rest-vs-in-flight.statement: Zscaler's DSPM product page describes the two separately in its FAQ: DSPM protects data, both local and in the cloud, against unauthorized access, misuse or theft by continuously monitoring, updating and refining security measures, while cloud DLP monitors and inspects data on a network to prevent data exfiltration; the page says DSPM is natively integrated with the Zscaler Data Security platform.

quotes: DSPM works to protect data—both local and in the cloud—against unauthorized access, misuse, or theft by continuously monitoring, updating, and refining security measures.
Cloud DLP monitors and inspects data on a network to prevent data exfiltration stemming from cyberattacks like phishing, ransomware, and insider threats.
Natively integrated with the Zscaler Data Security platform, it enables you to fully understand and control all your data on a single platform.

no-client-surface.statement: No vendored client covers DSPM: the Go and Python SDKs, the Terraform providers, the Ansible collections, the MCP server, the OneAPI Postman collection and the captured Automate contract have no DSPM service.

quotes: used in your server-side code to interact with the Zscaler API platform across multiple products such as:

no-client-surface.conditions: Rests on an absence. The Python README's product list (introduced by the quoted line) names no DSPM API, and at the pins `git grep -i dspm` finds no DSPM code in the Go or Python SDKs, the ZIA, ZPA, ZCC or ZTC providers, the Ansible collections or the MCP server (the only hits are base64 test data); the one Postman match is not a DSPM endpoint family.

marketing-scope.statement: Zscaler's DSPM product page says it covers all data stores, including IaaS, SaaS, on-premises and endpoint, discovers and classifies structured and unstructured data across IaaS, SaaS, on-premises, AI and endpoint, and finds sensitive data across hybrid and multicloud environments.

quotes: Zscaler DSPM takes an AI-powered, unified approach to ensure strong data hygiene across all data stores, including IaaS, SaaS, on-premises, endpoint, and more.
Leverage AI to automatically discover and classify structured and unstructured data across IaaS, SaaS, on-premises, AI, and endpoint.
Find and protect sensitive data across hybrid and multicloud environments with fully integrated, AI-powered data security posture management (DSPM).

guide-steps.statement: The step-by-step guide lists nine configuration steps: set up your account, set up the DLP engines and define sensitive data, onboard cloud accounts, configure scan settings, users, business units, data posture policies, alert rules, and 3rd-party integrations and notifications.

quotes: Step 1: Set up Your Account
Step 2: Set up the DLP Engines and Define Sensitive Data
Step 3: Onboard Cloud Accounts
Step 4: Configure Scan Settings
Step 5: Configure Users
Step 6: Configure Business Units
Step 7: Configure the Data Posture Policies
Step 8: Configure Alert Rules
Step 9: Configure 3rd-Party Integrations and Notifications

guide-registration.statement: After the organization is provisioned for DSPM, an email arrives to complete the registration.

quotes: After your organization is provisioned for DSPM, you receive an email to complete the registration.

guide-dlp-engines.statement: The step-by-step configuration guide says DSPM uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA) to classify data types.

quotes: DSPM uses predefined DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA) to classify data types.

guide-cloud-providers.statement: The step-by-step configuration guide says AWS organizations, Microsoft Azure tenants or GCP organizations can be onboarded into DSPM, which then monitors the data in the cloud accounts for vulnerabilities and threats.

quotes: You can onboard the Amazon Web Services (AWS) organizations, Microsoft Azure tenants, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) organizations into DSPM.
DSPM monitors the data in your cloud accounts for any vulnerabilities and threats

guide-scan-and-bu.statement: The step-by-step configuration guide says that after cloud accounts are onboarded, scan settings are configured, and DSPM scans the resources in the onboarded accounts, classifies the data, detects vulnerabilities and generates alerts; it also says accounts can be mapped to business units and user access can be restricted to specific business units (see dspm.roles:business-unit-definition).

quotes: After you have onboarded the cloud accounts, you need to configure the scan settings.
DSPM scans the resources (data stores, cloud storage, virtual machines, etc.) in your onboarded cloud accounts
classifies the data, detects vulnerabilities, and generates alerts
You can onboard your cloud accounts and map them to business units. You can restrict user access to specific business units.

guide-policies-alerts.statement: The step-by-step configuration guide says DSPM offers predefined data posture policies for compliance across multiple CSPs and also supports custom policies, and offers incident management by integrating with ITSM tools and cloud storage services.

quotes: DSPM offers predefined data posture policies to meet your organization's compliance requirements across multiple cloud service providers (CSPs).
You can also create custom policies.
DSPM offers incident management by integrating with IT Service Management (ITSM) tools and cloud storage services.

api-and-scanner-contract.title: Whether DSPM has an admin API, and the full scanner and orchestrator deployment contract
api-and-scanner-contract.detail: Unverified legacy statement: DSPM programmable or admin API details and the scanner/orchestrator setup contract are unresolved. Now known: scans run through a local scan orchestrator deployed in the onboarded account (dspm.scanning:orchestrator), and the supported-data-stores page lists scan instance types per store. Still open: any DSPM API, and the orchestrator's network and permission requirements, which the help site covers in pages not captured here (Understanding Orchestrator, Understanding Scanner Instances).
api-and-scanner-contract.blocks: telling an operator whether DSPM findings or configuration can be automated, and what the in-account scanner needs
